title: Isandro and the Hollow
premise: Hazel Sandoval, a cartographer who once mapped the unmapped realms and now hides as a charm-seller in the magic-outlawed city of Vessengard, is found by a child named Isandro who speaks the First Tongue — a language that predates kingdoms and can unmake bindings. The child leads Hazel to discover that King Aldric has been hollowed out, his body worn by a crown-born entity called the Regent, which sustains itself by outlawing the very magic it feeds on. Hunted by the Crown's inquisitors and betrayed by Hazel's old mentor, who helped forge the Regent, they must reach the throne room before the Binding Rite seals the king permanently. In the end, Hazel chooses truth over loyalty to their mentor, speaks the Unbinding through Isandro's voice, and frees Aldric — but the cost is Hazel's own maps, memories of every realm they ever charted, traded to close the door the Regent came through.
about_author: Zephyrine Nakamura is a former archivist of endangered languages who writes fantasy about the words we lose and the ones that refuse to die. They live between two coastlines and insist both are fictional.

chapters.title: The Child at the Door
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Three years into selling illegal charms disguised as trinkets, Hazel opens their door to a mud-streaked child speaking a language no living scholar knows — yet Hazel understands it, because they charted its homeland long ago. The beat: dread wrapped in wonder, as the past Hazel buried knocks politely.

chapters.title: Charms for a City That Forbids
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Flashback braided with present: how Vessengard outlawed magic, how Hazel survived by shrinking wonders into pocket-sized lies. Isandro follows Hazel through the market, and the child's mere presence makes dead charms flicker alive. The beat: the suffocating weight of a life built on small concealments.

chapters.title: What the King Wears
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, rendered in his strange, literal cadence. The child reveals he was sent from the Hollow — the space beneath the crown — to find 'the one who draws doors.' He shows Hazel a vision: King Aldric's eyes, empty as wells, something else looking out. The beat: horror arriving gently, through a child's certainty.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Kindness
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Inquisitor Maren Vale, who has suspected Hazel for years, offers a bargain: deliver the child, and Hazel's crimes are forgotten. Hazel refuses — and realizes refusing has painted a target on them both. The beat: the first true choice, made too fast to regret properly.

chapters.title: The Mentor in the Tower
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel seeks Odile Ferran, the cartographer-mentor who taught them to map realms — and finds her wearing an inquisitor's gray. Odile admits she helped bind the Regent to Aldric decades ago, believing it would end the realm-wars. The beat: loyalty cracking against the truth that your hero built the cage.

chapters.title: Down Through the Undercity
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Fleeing Odile's soldiers, Hazel and Isandro descend into Vessengard's drowned undercity, where outlawed magic survives in exile communities. An old river-priest reads Isandro's tongue and weeps: it is the language of making, and the child is not a messenger but a key. The beat: fragile hope among the discarded.

chapters.title: The Hollow Opens
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The Regent, sensing its key nearby, reaches through Isandro's dreams, showing him the Hollow — a kingdom-sized absence where a realm used to be, devoured to birth the crown. Isandro wakes screaming in a language that now burns Hazel's ears. The beat: the enemy revealed as hunger with a face.

chapters.title: A Map With No Edges
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. To enter the palace on coronation eve, Hazel must do the forbidden thing: draw a living map, one that rewrites space as it's walked. It will consume pieces of the cartographer. Odile intercepts them — not to arrest, but to beg Hazel to let the binding stand, because unmaking the Regent unmakes the peace. The beat: the mentor's grief reframing the villain's logic.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, climax. Hazel walks the living map into the throne room mid-Rite; Isandro speaks the First Tongue while Hazel anchors him; the Regent tears free of Aldric and offers Hazel everything they've lost if they'll just stop drawing. Hazel answers by finishing the map — and the Regent, given edges at last, can be closed inside them. The beat: truth spoken plainly, at terrible price.

chapters.title: Cartography of What Remains
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, resolution. King Aldric, freed but broken, abolishes the magical prohibition; Odile turns herself over to a court Hazel refuses to attend. Hazel remembers none of the realms they charted — but Isandro stays, teaching Hazel their own past one story at a time, beginning with a door drawn in chalk. The beat: quiet, earned tenderness; identity rebuilt rather than recovered.
